== Background information ==
=== Title ===
* {{D|6|April|2022}}: Title publicly revealed by [[Wil Wheaton]] in {{TRR|Surrender}}.
* {{Latin episodes}}
* The spelling of "Võx" in the title is unusual, as the Latin word would usually be written either with a macron – ''vōx'' – or more commonly with no diacritic, such as in {{ENT|Vox Sola}}.
* This is the second of three ''Star Trek'' series episodes with the word "vox" in the title.

=== Production ===
* Two starship classes from ''[[Star Trek Online]]'' make their on-screen debut in this episode, namely the {{Class|Alita}} and the {{Class|Edison}}. Vessels of the {{Class|Odyssey}}, {{Class|Pathfinder}} and {{Class|Pioneer}} also appear for the first time, after previously making their debuts as photographs and computer graphics earlier in the season.
* Ship names, registry numbers and class names for several starships seen during [[Frontier Day]] were provided by [[Dave Blass]] on Twitter and Instagram.
* The {{USS|Enterprise|NCC-1701-D|-D}} bridge was an entirely new set. The only legacy component of the set was the dedication plaque which was an original prop used during the filming of seasons 5-7 of {{S|TNG}}. The plaque was removed from the set each day after filming, for fear of it being stolen. {{Twitter|DaveBlass/status/1647253218823380992}} {{Twitter|lizklocz/status/1647732762496090112}}

=== Cast and characters ===
* [[Elizabeth Dennehy]] reprises her role of [[Elizabeth Shelby]], now a [[fleet admiral]] and in command of the {{USS|Enterprise|NCC-1701-F|-F}} during its decommissioning. Shelby made a non-speaking appearance in {{LD|An Embarrassment Of Dooplers}} and was last portrayed by Dennehy in {{TNG|The Best of Both Worlds, Part II}}. Her given name, Elizabeth, is provided for the first time in this episode, although it had already been used for many years in novels and comics since the character's first appearance.
* [[Alice Krige]] reprises her role of  the [[Borg Queen]], albeit only as a voice over. Krige last voiced a holographic recreation of the Queen in {{LD|I, Excretus}} and last appeared as the Queen in {{VOY|Endgame}}. This also marks the actual prime timeline's Queen's first appearance since "Endgame", as the Queen prominently seen during [[PIC Season 2|season 2]] of ''Picard'' originated from an alternate timeline.
* [[Jane Edwina Seymour]] takes over the physical portrayal of the Borg Queen, although the character is only seen briefly from behind in this episode. Seymour is the fourth actor to portray the Queen, following Alice Krige, [[Annie Wersching]], and [[Susanna Thompson]].
* The late [[Majel Barrett Roddenberry|Majel Barrett]] is credited as the [[Enterprise Computer|''Enterprise'' Computer]]. Majel Barrett Roddenberry voiced most Starfleet computers on {{S|TNG}}, {{S|DS9}} and {{S|VOY}} and provided her last voice overs as the computer for {{Film|XI}}, posthumously released in 2009. The credit in this episode is unusual, as no new audio by Barrett Roddenberry was used. Instead, lines were taken partly from {{TNG|Chain Of Command, Part II}} and from {{TNG|Starship Mine}}.

=== Continuity ===
* This episode sees the return of the [[Borg]] as a major threat to the [[United Federation of Planets|Federation]]. It is also revealed that the rogue [[Changeling]]s cooperated with the Borg to infiltrate [[Starfleet]] and orchestrate the downfall of the Federation. The Borg last directly attacked [[Earth]] in {{Film|8}} and were not seen as a major antagonist since {{VOY|Endgame}}, although they have made appearances in several later episodes.
* [[Jean-Luc Picard]]'s [[assimilation]] in [[2366]] left his [[DNA]] altered and transformed a part of his [[parietal lobe]], as already stated in {{TNG|The Best of Both Worlds, Part II}}. This episode reveals that the alterations worked like a biological receiver of Borg signals and caused symptoms which were later misdiagnosed as [[Irumodic Syndrome]].
* Picard passed his biological Borg traits on to [[Jack Crusher]], who therefore possesses a natural connection to the [[Borg Collective|Collective]], much like his father. Jack, however, also possesses the unique ability to transmit a Borg signal to other humanoids, explaining his ability to seize control of people as showcased throughout the season. Amplified by the [[Borg Queen]] and her ship, this signal is used to assimilate young officers across the gathered fleet whose DNA had been altered by manipulation of [[transporter]]s by the changeling infiltrators.
* [[Frontier Day]] is revealed to celebrate the 250th anniversary of the launch of {{NX|Enterprise}} (NX-01) in April [[2151]]. This was previously confirmed on Twitter by [[Dave Blass]] and [[Terry Matalas]] after Frontier Day posters were first seen earlier in the season in {{E|The Next Generation}}. Though this episode does not give a specific day of the month, Matalas tweeted that Frontier Day was specifically the 13th of April. {{twitter|TerryMatalas/status/1644904720862150657}}
* As stated by Admiral Shelby, the launch of ''Enterprise'' is considered to be the origin of modern [[Starfleet]] by the early [[25th century]]. Although Earth's Starfleet had already existed by the [[2130s]] and the [[United Federation of Planets]] would not be founded until [[2161]], Terry Matalas pointed out the significance of [[Jonathan Archer]]'s mission including a multispecies command crew (i.e. [[T'Pol]] and [[Phlox]]) in 2151, which would be highly respected by future generations. {{twitter|TerryMatalas/status/1644911469430177793}}
* As stated in this and previous episodes, all (or almost all) of Starfleet's active starships gather in [[Earth]] orbit for Frontier Day celebrations. If taken at face value, the fleet showcase allows several observations of the state of Starfleet at the beginning of the 25th century:
** The bulk of Starfleet is comprised of ships of the {{Class|Akira}}, {{Class|Alita}}, {{Class|Defiant}}, {{Class|Duderstadt}}, {{Class|Echelon}}, {{Class|Edison}}, {{Class|Excelsior II}}, {{Class|Gagarin}}, {{Class|Inquiry}}, {{Class|Luna}}, {{Class|Odyssey}}, {{Class|Nova}}, {{Class|Pathfinder}}, {{Class|Reliant}}, {{Class|Ross}}, {{Class|Sagan}}, {{Class|Sovereign}}, {{Class|Steamrunner}}, and {{Class|Sutherland}}.
** Starfleet seems to have significantly renewed the core of its fleet since the mid-[[2370s|2380s]]. The oldest shown starship-class appears to be the {{Class|Defiant}}, developed after [[2366]]. Old mainstays of the fleet, such as the {{Class|Galaxy}}, {{Class|Nebula}}, {{Class|Excelsior}}, {{Class|California}}, or {{Class|Miranda}} are no longer present. In part, this renewal seems to have been a preparation for the implementation of [[fleet formation mode]].
** The overall number of active starships seems to be lower in [[2401]] than it was at the height of the [[Dominion War]]. [[Operation Return]] saw the gathering of over six hundred Federation ships to retake [[Deep Space 9]] in [[2374]], ({{DS9|Favor the Bold}}) while 339 ships are part of Fleet Formation mode in this episode. Over a century earlier, in [[2257]], Starfleet was stated to contain seven thousand active ships, although this number may have included small crafts. ({{DIS|Perpetual Infinity}})
** Many of the approximately ninety {{Class|Inquiry}} starships seen in {{E|Et in Arcadia Ego, Part 2}} appear to be engaged elsewhere or are no longer in service.
* While the fate of the {{USS|Enterprise|NCC-1701-E|-E}} is not revealed, [[Geordi La Forge]]'s remarks indicate that the ship has been lost or destroyed. [[Worf]] appears to have been involved in the ship's demise, although he insists that he is not to blame for its fate. The characters could be referencing the events of {{PRO|Supernova, Part 2}}, in which a {{Class|Sovereign}} starship bearing the ''Enterprise''-E's markings was attacked by the [[living construct]] and later seen adrift after sustaining severe damage.
* This episode confirms that Captain Worf was the first Klingon to command a Federation starship.
* The {{USS|Enterprise|NCC-1701-D|-D}} is revealed to have been restored for twenty years by Geordi La Forge at the [[Fleet Museum]], following its partial destruction and crash in [[2371]] ({{Film|7}}). That the saucer section had been lifted off [[Veridian III]] and brought to the museum was first revealed in {{E|The Star Gazer}}, written on one of the placards seen at [[Starfleet Academy]].
* La Forge's work on the ''Enterprise''-D included restoring the bridge to its [[2370]] configuration, as seen during [[TNG Season 7|season 7]] of {{S|TNG}}. Several alterations seen in {{Film|7}}, such as additional consoles and raised sections, were no longer present.
* Picard ordering Data to set the ''Enterprise''-D on a course for Earth at maximum warp to confront the Borg echoes a similar line in {{Film|8}} when Picard ordered [[Lt.]] {{Dis|Hawk|Lieutenant}} to set the ''Enterprise''-E on a course for Earth at maximum warp to confront the Borg in the [[Battle of Sector 001]].

[[Nova Fleet]] {{small|(formerly)}} |occupation = [[Commanding officer]], [[Cosmia's ship|Orion interceptor]] |status = Active |datestatus = 2381 |actor = [[Fred Tatasciore]] }} '''Risik''' was a [[male]] [[Orion]] [[plunder sorter]] who served aboard [[Cosmia's ship]] during the late [[24th century]]. In [[2381]], Risik was working alongside [[D'Bora]] and [[L'Kar]] when he told them of his intention to get a [[chain]] [[tattoo]]. L'Kar told him that those had to be earned, and scoffed at his claim of being capable of rising above his present station. Risik then stated that he wanted to install [[metal]] {{dis|bolt|fastener}}s on his head like their crewmate [[Maleer]], prompting L'Kar and D'Bora to mock him for being an unoriginal "[[plagiarism|plagiarist]]". Shortly after, Risik was summoned to the [[bridge]] as their ship had encountered [[Nova One|a small vessel]]. Risik was in fact colluding with the vessel's [[pilot]], [[Nick Locarno]], to effect a [[mutiny]]. He surreptitiously deactivated his ship's systems, and with Locarno's aid overthrew his [[captain]] and [[first officer]], whom he marooned on [[Sherbal V]]. ({{LD|Something Borrowed, Something Green|The Inner Fight|Old Friends, New Planets}}) Later that year, having joined Locarno's [[Nova Fleet]], Risik was among those who pursued [[Beckett Mariner]] in the [[Detrion system]]. However, he was unwilling to follow her vessel into a level-7 [[ion storm]]. When the [[trynar shield]] around the system was subsequently breached by the {{USS|Cerritos}}, Risik decided to abandon Locarno and flee. The rest of Nova Fleet, disillusioned with the increasingly unstable and controlling Locarno even before the shield was breached, followed suit.
